title: Product management on the AI exponential
author: Cat Wu, Head of Product for Claude Code, Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's own Claude Code product lead explains how she splits work across Claude.ai (thinking partner), Claude Code (prototypes, evals, scripts) and Cowork (everything else), then gives four concrete process shifts: short self-directed experiments instead of locked roadmaps, demos and evals instead of docs, revisiting shipped features when a new model lands, and keeping implementations simple so model upgrades drop in cleanly.
who_for: A PM who already uses Claude daily and wants to see how a team at Anthropic actually organises around it, with real examples (todo lists, plugins, Claude Code with Chrome).
skip_if: You want click-by-click instructions. There are no prompts or templates here, only process advice, and the framing assumes a fast-moving software team with its own roadmap.
notes: First-party and specific about failure modes, which is rare in this space. Embeds a short video (youtube.com/embed/91AJ0cpgLlQ).

title: Product Management Plugin (official Anthropic plugin)
author: Anthropic
summary: The install page for Anthropic's own PM plugin. It adds six slash commands to Cowork or Claude Code: /write-spec, /roadmap-update, /stakeholder-update, /synthesize-research, /competitive-brief and /metrics-review, and it can pull context from Slack, Linear, Asana, Notion, Figma, Amplitude and Intercom over MCP.
who_for: A PM on a Claude Pro or Max plan who wants working PM commands in one click rather than writing their own prompts.
skip_if: You do not use Cowork or Claude Code, or your company blocks connectors — without MCP connections you have to paste all context by hand, which removes most of the advantage.
notes: Marked 'Anthropic Verified'. The page showed an install count of 0 on 2026-08-21, which looks like a display bug rather than real adoption.

title: knowledge-work-plugins: product-management (source and README)
author: Anthropic
summary: The readable source behind the official PM plugin: seven skill files covering feature specs, roadmap management, stakeholder comms, research synthesis, competitive analysis, metrics tracking and product brainstorming, plus worked command transcripts in the README. The skills carry real opinions, for example 'If everything is P0, nothing is P0'.
who_for: A PM who wants to read what Anthropic thinks good PM output looks like, then fork the skills and swap in their own templates and company context.
skip_if: You just want the plugin to work — install it from claude.com/plugins/product-management instead and never open GitHub.
notes: Apache-2.0. Anthropic's own README says the plugins are 'starting points' and the value comes from customising them, which is honest.

title: Claude Code 101 (Anthropic Academy)
author: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's free self-paced course on Claude Code: installation across terminal, VS Code, JetBrains and Desktop, the explore-plan-code-commit loop, context management with /compact and /clear, CLAUDE.md project memory, subagents, skills, MCP and hooks. Ends with a quiz and certificate.
who_for: A PM who has decided to learn Claude Code properly and wants the mechanics from the source rather than from a newsletter.
skip_if: You are not comfortable with a code editor and command line — the stated prerequisites assume both, and the course is written for developers, so every example is a coding example with no PM framing.
notes: Free, hosted on Skilljar. Only needs an email, not an Anthropic account. Course length is not stated on the page; half-day is an estimate from the curriculum size.

title: How Anthropic uses Claude in Product Management (video)
author: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's own video on how its product managers use Claude. It is the companion to Cat Wu's 'Product management on the AI exponential' post and is embedded at the end of it.
who_for: A PM who prefers watching people work to reading about it, and wants a first-party account rather than a course seller's.
skip_if: You have already read the Cat Wu article — the video covers the same ground, and I could not confirm its runtime or publication date.
notes: Found embedded in claude.com/blog/product-management-on-the-ai-exponential. Runtime and upload date unverified.

title: Claude for Product Management (official tutorial)
author: Anthropic
summary: A five-minute Anthropic tutorial video showing examples of PM teams using Claude.ai. It is an overview of what is possible, not a workflow you can copy.
who_for: A PM who has never opened Claude and wants a short first look from the vendor before committing time.
skip_if: You already use Claude at all. Five minutes of examples will not teach you anything you cannot get from the plugin README, and the page shows no publication date.
notes: Possibly outdated. The embedded Vimeo asset (id 1018853967) predates Cowork, Skills and the current Claude Code, none of which are mentioned. Treat as a taster only.

title: Claude Code for Product Managers (free course, taught inside Claude Code)
author: Carl Vellotti (The Full Stack PM)
summary: A free 10-12 hour course you install by pasting one prompt into the Claude Desktop Code tab; Claude then teaches you interactively while you do real PM work on a fictional company called TaskFlow. Covers file operations, parallel agents, custom sub-agents (engineer, executive, user researcher), CLAUDE.md project memory, then PRD writing, funnel and A/B analysis, and competitive strategy.
who_for: A PM with no terminal experience who wants the single most complete free path from zero to competent with Claude Code, and who learns by doing rather than watching.
skip_if: You cannot commit 10-12 hours, or you do not have Claude Pro or Max — the course needs a paid plan to run. Also skip if you want a video course; there are no lecture videos.
notes: Free but requires Claude Pro or Max (about $20/month). Not affiliated with Anthropic — the author says so plainly. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Source at github.com/carlvellotti/free-ai-courses.

title: Write a PRD with Claude Code (Module 2.1)
author: Carl Vellotti (The Full Stack PM)
summary: A 45-60 minute exercise in four techniques: load full context with @-mentions, use Socratic questioning to sharpen your own thinking before writing, spin up three parallel agents to draft three strategic approaches, then run engineer, executive and user-researcher sub-agents over the draft. Includes a troubleshooting table for when the output feels generic.
who_for: A PM who already has Claude Code working and wants one concrete, repeatable PRD workflow today rather than a whole course.
skip_if: You have not done Modules 1.4 and 1.5 — the sub-agent steps assume agent files already exist in .claude/agents/, and the page will read as theory without them.
notes: The 'Don't' list is the best part: it explicitly warns against letting the AI write for you and against accepting the first draft.

title: Complete Guide to Claude Cowork (with 12 free interactive lessons)
author: Carl Vellotti (The Full Stack PM)
summary: A long reference guide to Cowork plus a downloadable 12-lesson course you run inside Cowork itself. The useful parts are the 'Done' framework for writing delegations, four copyable prompt templates, an inbox/processed/outputs folder pattern, and a blunt limitations section that says browser automation is hit or miss and connectors are unreliable.
who_for: A PM who wants Claude to produce real .xlsx and .pptx files from messy folders of research and notes, without touching a terminal.
skip_if: You mainly need code or a prototype — the guide itself tells you to use Claude Code for that. Also skip if you need current platform facts.
notes: Marked 'Last updated: January 2026' and is now partly stale: it says Cowork is macOS only and has no Projects, both of which have since changed. The prompt patterns and safety checklist still hold.

title: Claude Code for PMs: The Beginner's Guide
author: Paweł Huryn (The Product Compass)
summary: A zero-to-one setup path for PMs who have never used Cowork: install VS Code and the Claude Code extension, download a ready-made project template with a minimal CLAUDE.md and permissions, configure MCP connectors from claude.ai, and create your first skill by asking Claude to make one. Ends with an optional route to run Claude Code on free OpenRouter models.
who_for: A PM who wants the fastest correct setup, with a template to download instead of a blank folder.
skip_if: You already run Claude Code comfortably — this is installation and configuration, not PM craft, and the free-models section is a side quest most PMs should ignore.
notes: Free to read; the template download needs a free Substack signup. Names a live Anthropic bug (claude-code issue 36179) that blocks alternative models in the VS Code extension, which may be fixed by now.

title: The Guide to Claude Code for PMs
author: Paweł Huryn (The Product Compass)
summary: The Cowork-to-Claude-Code transition guide. The free half covers what genuinely changes: connectors carry over automatically, Auto Memory replaces the old cross-session workaround, Plan Mode lets you explore a codebase without touching it, message queuing, visible context usage, and /effort control. The paid half holds the PM power moves and the 'where Cowork is still better' caveats.
who_for: A PM already productive in Cowork who keeps hitting its ceiling and wants to know exactly what the move to Claude Code buys them.
skip_if: You have never used Cowork — the whole framing is 'you are already 70% there', so start with the same author's beginner guide instead. Also skip if you will not pay for the newsletter, since the honest-caveats section is behind the paywall.
notes: Paywalled after section 3, with a 7-day free trial. Free portion alone is still worth reading.

title: Claude Code for Product Managers (Sachin Rekhi)
author: Sachin Rekhi (ex-Head of Product, LinkedIn Sales Navigator)
summary: Five real skills a practising PM built and uses: critiquing a product strategy against his own frameworks, scraping competitor pricing pages with a browser agent because deep research returns stale prices, transcribing and cross-synthesising customer interview videos, answering data questions in plain English via generated SQL, and writing release notes from a commit URL in his product's existing voice.
who_for: A PM who wants to see what a skill library looks like when someone has fed it their own frameworks, not generic templates.
skip_if: You want the build instructions — the free portion stops exactly where 'Getting Started' begins, so without a subscription you get inspiration and no method.
notes: Paywalled with a 7-day trial. Explicitly a promotion for his Reforge AI Productivity course, which he discloses up front. Companion video at youtube.com/watch?v=zsAAaY8a63Q.

title: Agent-native Product Management (Every's guide)
author: Marcus Moretti, GM of Spiral at Every
summary: A working method from someone who runs a whole product alone. Two installable skills are described in full: /ce-strategy interviews you into a five-part strategy.md based on Rumelt's Good Strategy Bad Strategy, and /ce:product-pulse builds a one-page daily metrics report from PostHog, Sentry, Stripe and a read-only database, saving every run to a folder that becomes the product's memory.
who_for: A solo PM, founder or small-team owner who already writes specs and wants to stop writing tickets entirely and move to strategy-plus-metrics-loop.
skip_if: Your product is not instrumented — the guide says outright to stop reading and go set up analytics first. Also skip if you work in a large org with a shared tracker and process you cannot change.
notes: Free to read in full, unlike the companion essay at every.to/source-code/claude-code-for-product-managers which is paywalled. Honest 'What's not included' section names prioritisation and pulse comparison as gaps.

title: compound-engineering-plugin (Every)
author: Every Media (Kieran Klaassen, Marcus Moretti)
summary: The open-source Claude Code plugin holding the ce-strategy and ce-product-pulse skills from Every's PM guide, alongside ce-ideate, ce-brainstorm and ce-plan. Installed with /plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.
who_for: A PM who read Every's guide and wants the actual skills rather than a description of them.
skip_if: You have not read the guide first — the skills are interview-driven and the guide explains what a good answer looks like. I did not inspect the repo contents, only the install instructions quoted in the guide.
notes: Agent-agnostic per Every's description, not Claude-only. Contents unverified.

title: Claude Cowork for Product Managers: A Working Guide
author: Stuart Miller (Haverin)
summary: Short and unusually blunt. Argues folder hygiene beats prompt quality, gives one complete working SKILL.md for research synthesis with no-fabricated-quotes rules, and then spends a whole section on where Cowork breaks: rubber-stamping plans, fuzzy deletion instructions, scheduled tasks drifting against changed folders, connectors failing silently, and the agent confabulating facts about its own behaviour.
who_for: A PM who is about to point Cowork at real work files and wants to know the failure modes before they hit them.
skip_if: You want breadth — this is one person's opinionated method, not a survey, and the client-confidentiality section may not match your legal situation.
notes: The author states the piece was generated with Claude and checked against Anthropic references, and tells you not to treat it as authoritative. Verify the platform claims yourself. Current as of May 2026 by the author's own statement.

title: Claude Code for Product Managers (Builder.io)
author: Vishwas Gopinath, Builder.io
summary: Setup plus six PM use cases (PRD to prototype, codebase exploration in Plan Mode, CSV analysis, documentation, research synthesis, MCP integrations), then a genuinely useful section on where it falls short: a complexity ceiling past simple tasks, MCP servers that disconnect and need re-auth, the last 20 percent of editing that needs codebase literacy, and no way to share work with the team.
who_for: A PM who wants one short honest orientation piece before deciding whether Claude Code is worth learning.
skip_if: You dislike vendor content — the last third pivots into a Builder.io pitch, and the 'limitations' are framed as problems Builder.io solves.
notes: Accurate on prices as of publication (Pro $20/month, Max from $100/month). Free, no signup.

title: How to Use Claude Code as a Product Manager
author: George Nurijanian (prodmgmt.world)
summary: A 25-minute walkthrough with two fully worked PM workflows (a clickable prototype and an automated competitor pricing table), plus the parts most guides skip: a 'baby steps' framework against spec-dumping, context poisoning and the $40 session trap, /cost /compact /clear, when to switch to Opus, and a 30-minute protocol for aligning Claude to a new codebase.
who_for: A PM who is past setup and keeps getting mediocre or expensive results, and wants the operating discipline that fixes it.
skip_if: You dislike before-and-after cost tables — the time-saving numbers here are the author's own estimates, not measured, and the page repeatedly sells his $99 PM OS product.
notes: Originally published December 2025, updated 2026-04-24. Treat the original date as a warning: check any command syntax against current Claude Code docs.

title: Claude for Product Managers: Synthesizing User Research
author: Enterpret
summary: One workflow done properly. Gives a complete copy-paste synthesis prompt with five required outputs (patterns with confidence levels, contradictions, confirmation versus challenge, what is missing, explicit uncertainty), plus a three-turn validation loop that challenges Claude's groupings, asks for the inverse finding, and demands the strongest quotes.
who_for: A PM sitting on 5-10 interview transcripts who wants synthesis rather than a tidy summary, and who wants to catch confident misreads before they reach a roadmap deck.
skip_if: Your research repository is larger than about 10 interviews per run — the guide admits quality drops past that and then steers you toward paid tooling, including its own MCP server.
notes: Vendor content, but the prompt and validation loop stand on their own and the article names the scaling limits honestly before pitching.

title: Top 7 Claude Skills for Product Managers
author: Stephen Thoemmes, Snyk
summary: The clearest available map of PM skill collections, with install commands, licences, star counts and what is actually inside each one. It also disambiguates CLAUDE.md, slash commands, MCP servers, connectors, skills and plugins, which almost nobody else does, and closes with a supply-chain warning backed by Snyk's own scan of 3,984 published skills.
who_for: A PM choosing which skill pack to install, and anyone who has been confused about how skills, MCP and CLAUDE.md differ.
skip_if: You only want Anthropic's official plugin — entries 5 to 7 are book-derived frameworks (JTBD, Hooked, CRO) with only 88 stars, and the security framing is Snyk marketing its own product.
notes: Security finding worth keeping: Snyk reports 13.4% of scanned skills contained at least one critical issue. Publication date is not shown on the page; skill 'last updated' dates cited are January-February 2026.

title: PM Claude Code Setup (free CLAUDE.md, 6 skills, 4 templates)
author: Aakash Gupta (Product Growth)
summary: A drop-in Claude Code config: a deliberately short CLAUDE.md (under 60 lines, because Claude follows short instructions better), six skills (prd-writer, competitive-analysis, launch-checklist, metrics-definer, sprint-planner, user-research) and four templates. The README's operating advice is the real value: chain sub-agent reviews, use @ references instead of pasting, /clear between unrelated tasks, cap sessions at about 50 exchanges, and a troubleshooting section for when skills do not trigger.
who_for: A PM who wants a working Claude Code setup in about 60 seconds and a list of the mistakes that cause bad output.
skip_if: You want the full system — this is deliberately a teaser for the author's $49 paid PM OS, and the skills ship with generic examples you must replace with your own product's before they beat plain prompting.
notes: Free and standalone despite the upsell. The troubleshooting section (skills not triggering, CLAUDE.md ignored past ~150 lines) is the most reusable part.

title: PM Operating System (Aakash Gupta)
author: Aakash Gupta (Product Growth)
summary: The paid version of the free setup above: a CLAUDE.md the author says he iterated on more than 100 times, a context library, 41 skills, 7 sub-agent reviewer personas (engineer, designer, exec, legal and others) and templates for launches, roadmaps, OKRs and retros.
who_for: A PM who has already used the free setup, hit its limits, and would rather buy a tuned configuration than spend weekends building one.
skip_if: You have not yet used the free repo — start there. The sales page also opens with 'Claude Code with Opus-4.6 is basically AGI', which is exactly the hype this space is full of, and the time-saving claims are unmeasured.
notes: Cohort-free product. $49 one-time on Gumroad (growthpioneer.gumroad.com/l/pmos), or bundled in a $250/year Founders plan. Price checked 2026-08-21.

title: Product-Manager-Skills (Dean Peters)
author: Dean Peters
summary: A PM skills framework of roughly 49 skills and 6 commands built on established PM methods, installable as a Claude Code plugin marketplace and readable in Cowork. Ships with a START_HERE guide, a catalogue, and separate docs for using the skills versus building your own.
who_for: A PM who wants breadth across templates, finance metrics, career frameworks and stakeholder tools from a long-time PM writer, and who likes reading skill source before running it.
skip_if: You want something curated — the catalogue is large and unopinionated about what to install first, and it overlaps heavily with the official Anthropic plugin. Version was v0.79 on 2026-08-21, so expect churn.
notes: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so check the non-commercial clause before using it inside a company. Distilled from the same author's product-manager-prompts repo.

title: PM Skills Marketplace (Paweł Huryn)
author: Paweł Huryn (The Product Compass)
summary: 68 PM skills and 42 chained workflows across 9 installable plugins, from /discover and /strategy to /write-prd, /red-team-prd, /plan-launch and /north-star. Skills encode named methods (Teresa Torres, Marty Cagan, Alberto Savoia, Roger Martin), and commands chain them so each one suggests the next. Includes install paths for Cowork, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor.
who_for: A PM who wants guided workflows with real frameworks behind them rather than prompt templates, and who works in Cowork as a non-developer.
skip_if: You are new to Claude — the author's own advice applies, start with no skills and add one when a real task forces it, because every installed skill costs context even when unused.
notes: MIT licensed. Includes a PowerShell workaround for a known Cowork VM failure on Windows (claude-code issue 27010). Companion repo: phuryn/pm-brain.

title: Lenny's Product Skills for Claude Code
author: Refound AI, from Lenny's Podcast
summary: 86 skills distilled from 100-plus episodes of Lenny's Podcast, covering discovery, PRDs, prioritisation, growth loops, pricing, retention, hiring, difficult conversations and career moves. Installs in one line with npx skills add, or by copying folders into .claude/skills/.
who_for: A PM who already trusts the advice from Shreyas Doshi, Marty Cagan and Elena Verna and wants it available as workflows instead of as podcast episodes.
skip_if: You need current product mechanics — these are people-and-craft skills, not Claude skills. About half the catalogue (hiring, sales comp, fundraising) is irrelevant to an individual contributor PM, and the skills are third-party interpretations, not authored by the podcast guests.
notes: MIT licensed. Not an official Lenny's Newsletter product; built by Refound AI from public episodes.

title: Ralph: PRD skill plus autonomous implementation loop
author: snarktank, based on Geoffrey Huntley's Ralph pattern
summary: Two skills that connect specification to shipping: /prd runs a conversational PRD workflow that asks lettered multiple-choice clarifying questions and produces stories sized for one agent session with verifiable acceptance criteria, and /ralph converts that PRD into a JSON plan an agent loop executes story by story until everything passes.
who_for: A PM or founder who owns both the spec and the build, and wants specs written so an agent can actually execute them.
skip_if: You work with an engineering team on a real production codebase. Handing an autonomous loop your repo is not a good idea, and nothing here reviews the code it writes. I read a detailed third-party description of the repo, not the skill files.
notes: MIT licensed, about 9,755 stars per Snyk's February 2026 count. Contents unverified by me.

title: Claude Code for PMs Certification (Product School)
author: Product School
summary: A live, instructor-led certification with an eight-module curriculum: Claude Code mental model, automated discovery from transcripts and datasets, prototyping and validation, working across the product triad, data-backed decisions, documentation and updates, operationalising the habit, and building a personal agent stack. Class size is stated as about 20 students.
who_for: A working senior PM whose employer will pay, who wants live instruction and a recognised certificate rather than self-study.
skip_if: You are paying yourself. $2,999 buys the same ground as Carl Vellotti's free course plus the Anthropic plugin, and Product School itself says you should complete its AI Product Management certification first, which is another course. Not for new PMs — the page says so.
notes: Price on 2026-08-21: $2,999 single certification; $3,999/year Pro (2 courses); $4,999/year Unlimited (10 courses). Start dates are not listed on the page. Instructor described as a practitioner from Intuit.

title: Claude Code for Product Managers (Maven, Aman Khan and Eric Xiao)
author: Aman Khan (Arize) and Eric Xiao
summary: A two-week live cohort of 13 sessions built around building during class: package your workflows into skills with skill-creator, connect skills to MCP tools, ground brainstorming in a real codebase, use agents as a UX designer for storyboards and wireframes, manage agent memory and sub-agents, and generate release notes and marketing copy from your own PRs.
who_for: A PM who learns best live, with office hours three times a week and a peer cohort, and who wants to go from chatbot user to agent operator in two weeks.
skip_if: You need it now or you need a price — the cohort was sold out on 2026-08-21 with no price shown, only a waitlist. The sales page is also almost entirely testimonial quotes, several of which lean on replacing colleagues, which is worth reading sceptically.
notes: Sold out on 2026-08-21; price not displayed. Rated 5.0 from 34 reviews. Listed schedule showed Week 1 starting 10 August 2026, so a past cohort. Three free recorded sessions are offered on the page. Commitment stated as 5 hours live plus 5 hours projects per week.

title: Production Ready Agentic AI PM Certification and Claude Cert Prep (Maven)
author: Mahesh Yadav, Agentic AI Institute
summary: A five-week live certification about building and shipping AI products rather than about Claude itself: RAG and agentic RAG, evals and LLM-as-judge, MCP, responsible AI guardrails, AI-native PRDs, and deployment across AWS, Azure and GCP, with Claude Code used as the build tool and prep for Anthropic's Claude certifications.
who_for: A PM who wants to move into AI product roles and needs a portfolio project, an eval story and interview preparation, not just better documents.
skip_if: You want to learn Claude for PM craft. Most of this is AI product management, and Claude is the vehicle. At $3,000 with a sales page built on testimonials, hiring screenshots and countdown urgency, the burden of proof is on the course, not on you.
notes: Price on 2026-08-21: $3,000. Next cohorts 29 August to 4 October 2026, then 9 January to 14 February 2027. Rated 4.8 from 603 reviews. Described as Maven's only Anthropic Claude Partner AI course. Commitment: 8 hours live plus 5 project plus 5 async per week.

title: Claude Code for Product Managers: Build and Ship with AI (Udemy)
author: Navdeep Yadav
summary: Just under two hours of video across 25 lectures that walk one PM path end to end: install Claude Code, use Plan Mode, build a to-do app with authentication, set environment variables, push to GitHub, deploy on Vercel with Neon and Clerk, then build a custom skill and finish with Claude Design for screens.
who_for: A PM who wants to watch one person deploy a real, live product start to finish before trying it themselves.
skip_if: You want PM craft rather than deployment. This is a build-and-ship course, not a specs, research or roadmap course, and two hours cannot go deep. Only 45 ratings, so the 4.5 score means little.
notes: Last updated 5/2026. 2,260 students, 4.5 from 45 ratings on 2026-08-21. Udemy list price was not shown to me; Udemy prices swing widely with sales, so check before buying. Requires a Claude Pro plan on top.

title: AI Productivity (Reforge)
author: Sachin Rekhi
summary: Four modules across four weeks covering prototyping, customer and data insights, product strategy and product execution, taught by the author of the Claude Code for PMs guide. Available on demand or as a live cohort with weekly sessions, a Slack channel and unlimited chat access to the host.
who_for: A PM or product leader whose company already pays for Reforge, and who wants one structured course across the whole PM workflow rather than scattered posts.
skip_if: You would be buying Reforge just for this. The page shows no price and no syllabus detail beyond four module titles, and the free preview material (the author's own Substack post) covers a fair share of the practical content.
notes: Next live cohort starts 20 October 2026, running weekly to 10 November 2026; enrolment was not yet open on 2026-08-21 (waitlist only). Price not shown on the page — Reforge sells by subscription. Reforge is now part of Miro.
